words.definition: to follow a rule or agreement exactly
examples: All members must adhere to the rules.

words.definition: the period after a bad event and its effects
examples: Many people lost their homes in the aftermath of the flood.

words.definition: a statement that someone has done something wrong, without proof
examples: He denied all the allegations.

words.definition: a comparison that shows how two things are similar
examples: The teacher used an analogy to explain the idea.

words.definition: a strong hope or wish to achieve something
examples: She has aspirations to become a doctor.

words.definition: to say something firmly
examples: He asserted that he was innocent.

words.definition: the freedom to make your own decisions
examples: Teachers want more autonomy in the classroom.

words.definition: a strong negative reaction by many people
examples: The new tax caused a public backlash.

words.definition: without hope, or cold and unpleasant
examples: The future looks bleak for the company.

words.definition: to make something stronger or more successful
examples: The win bolstered the team's confidence.

words.definition: to stop
examples: The factory ceased production last year.

words.definition: to happen at the same time
examples: My birthday coincides with a public holiday.

words.definition: to work with someone to produce something
examples: The two universities collaborated on the research.

words.definition: to begin (formal)
examples: The ceremony will commence at noon.

words.definition: to collect information and put it together
examples: We compiled a list of useful websites.

words.definition: to make something better by adding something that suits it
examples: The wine complements the fish perfectly.

words.definition: to consist of particular parts
examples: The course comprises five modules.

words.definition: to admit that something is true, often unwillingly
examples: He conceded that he had made a mistake.

words.definition: to form or be something
examples: Women constitute half of the workforce.

words.definition: to say the opposite of what someone has said
examples: His story contradicts what the witness said.

words.definition: in an opposite way
examples: Some people love the city; conversely, others prefer the countryside.

words.definition: a connection between two things
examples: There is a strong correlation between sleep and health.

words.definition: to control or limit something bad
examples: The government wants to curb inflation.

words.definition: to consider something in a particular way (formal)
examples: The plan was deemed too expensive.

words.definition: to take something important away from someone
examples: Lack of sleep deprives the brain of rest.

words.definition: to get something from something else
examples: Many English words derive from Latin.

words.definition: to invent a plan or method
examples: They devised a new way to save energy.

words.definition: to make information known publicly
examples: The company did not disclose the price.

words.definition: to change facts or shapes so they are no longer true or correct
examples: The newspaper distorted what he said.

words.definition: to start something new and important
examples: She embarked on a new career.

words.definition: to include a range of things
examples: The course encompasses history and politics.

words.definition: to make people obey a law or rule
examples: The police enforce the speed limit.

words.definition: to involve something as a necessary part
examples: The job entails a lot of travel.

words.definition: to become more serious or bigger
examples: The argument quickly escalated.

words.definition: to use power or influence
examples: Parents exert a strong influence on children.

words.definition: a system in which people are organized by rank
examples: She rose quickly through the company hierarchy.

words.definition: imagined as possible, not real
examples: Let's consider a hypothetical situation.

words.definition: to force a rule, tax or punishment on someone
examples: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.

words.definition: to form an opinion from the information you have
examples: What can you infer from the text?

words.definition: existing from birth
examples: Children have an innate ability to learn languages.

words.definition: to become involved in a situation to change it
examples: The teacher intervened to stop the fight.

words.definition: being a natural part of something
examples: Curiosity is intrinsic to learning.

words.definition: allowed by law, or fair and reasonable
examples: That's a legitimate question.

words.definition: to show something clearly
examples: The illness manifests itself as a rash.

words.definition: to control someone or something in a clever, often unfair way
examples: Advertisers try to manipulate our choices.

words.definition: ordinary and boring
examples: I spent the day doing mundane tasks.

words.definition: an idea or belief
examples: I reject the notion that money buys happiness.

words.definition: a person who is new to an activity
examples: This course is for complete novices.

words.definition: to help someone or something develop
examples: Good teachers nurture their students' talents.

words.definition: to balance one effect with an opposite one
examples: Higher prices were offset by higher wages.

words.definition: the beginning of something, especially something bad
examples: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.

words.definition: to be greater or more important than something else
examples: The benefits outweigh the risks.

words.definition: more important than anything else
examples: Safety is paramount.

words.definition: to continue to exist or to keep doing something
examples: If the pain persists, see a doctor.

words.definition: common in a particular place or time
examples: The disease is prevalent in hot countries.

words.definition: likely to suffer from or do something
examples: He is prone to headaches.

words.definition: to cause a reaction, especially anger
examples: His comments provoked an angry response.

words.definition: based on reason, not emotion
examples: There must be a rational explanation.

words.definition: an area of activity or interest
examples: That is beyond the realm of possibility.

words.definition: not needed, or having lost your job because it is no longer needed
examples: Remove any redundant words from your essay.

words.definition: to improve something by making small changes
examples: We need to refine our plan.

words.definition: very careful and thorough
examples: The drug went through rigorous testing.

words.definition: strong and unlikely to break or fail
examples: We need a robust system.

words.definition: at the same time
examples: Two events happened simultaneously.

words.definition: an opinion that is stated publicly
examples: What is your stance on this issue?

words.definition: to be caused by something
examples: Her fear stems from a childhood experience.

words.definition: happening after something else
examples: Subsequent research confirmed the results.

words.definition: to stop something from being seen, expressed or growing
examples: She tried to suppress a smile.

words.definition: to be better or greater than something
examples: The results surpassed our expectations.

words.definition: easily affected or influenced by something
examples: Children are more susceptible to infections.

words.definition: long and boring
examples: Filling in forms is tedious.

words.definition: a change from one state to another
examples: The transition to online classes was difficult.

words.definition: real but not immediately obvious
examples: We need to find the underlying cause.

words.definition: to support a law, decision or principle
examples: Judges must uphold the law.

words.definition: to use something (formal)
examples: We must utilize all available resources.

words.definition: able to work successfully
examples: Solar power is a viable alternative.

words.definition: to produce a result or crop
examples: The experiment yielded interesting results.
